briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A two-week ceasefire between the US and Iran, brokered by Pakistan and China, has been declared and is reportedly in effect, transitioning the conflict towards diplomatic negotiations starting April 10, 2026, in Islamabad. This pivotal development occurs amidst ongoing, widespread military operations across Iran, Lebanon, and the Gulf, including significant Israeli strikes against Hezbollah and Iranian missile/drone attacks on Gulf States and Israel, creating a highly volatile and uncertain situation regarding the scope and adherence to the truce.

IRAN
Despite the ceasefire announcement, Iran experienced significant military activity. Israeli Air Force (IAF) strikes targeted Iran, including the central production site for sonar and underwater detection systems in Shiraz, a naval cruise missile and air defense system manufacturing site in Karaj, and eight rail bridges and sections of roads used for military transport across Tehran, Karaj, Tabriz, Kashan, and Qom. The Lavan Island oil refinery was attacked around 10:00 local time, causing a fire but no casualties, and explosions were also reported on Sirri Island. Iran's Pasteur Institute was attacked, and the Rafi Niya synagogue in Tehran was damaged in a strike targeting a senior Iranian commander. Infrastructure damage included the Tabriz-Tehran highway, Yahyabad railway bridge in Kashan, a railway bridge in Karaj, and a bridge over the Sarkheh Hesar river in Rey. The Bushehr nuclear plant reportedly continued safely producing electricity despite nearby missile strikes.

Iran launched missile and drone attacks towards the UAE (17 ballistic missiles, 35 drones intercepted), Kuwait (28 drones intercepted, damaging vital oil facilities, power stations, and water desalination plants), Bahrain (6 missiles, 31 drones intercepted), and Saudi Arabia (attacking a key oil pipeline pumping station). Iranian officials stated these attacks on UAE and Kuwait were in response to the Lavan and Sirri Island refinery strikes. Iranian media reported that the Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered all military units to cease fire. The Supreme National Security Council declared Iran achieved a "great victory" by forcing the US to accept a 10-point plan for a ceasefire, asserting Iran's continued control over the Strait of Hormuz and acceptance of uranium enrichment. President Pezeshkian thanked Pakistan for mediation and stated the ceasefire was the "fruit of the blood of our martyred Leader Khamenei."

ISRAEL
Israel supported the two-week ceasefire with Iran but explicitly stated it does not include Lebanon, continuing its large-scale military operations against Hezbollah. The IDF launched its largest wave of airstrikes against Hezbollah since Operation Roaring Lion began, codenamed "Eternal Darkness." This involved 50 fighter jets dropping approximately 160 bombs on 100 Hezbollah targets within 10 minutes across Beirut (Dahieh), Beqaa Valley, and southern Lebanon (Sidon, Nabatieh, Tyre). Targets included command centers, intelligence headquarters, rocket and naval units, and assets of the Radwan Force and aerial unit. IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir vowed to continue striking Hezbollah "without interruption." The IDF also killed Muhammad Dawad, a Hamas explosives expert, in northern Gaza.

Despite the ceasefire announcement, Iran launched multiple ballistic missile attacks on southern and central Israel, triggering sirens in Tel Sheva, Beersheba, central Israel, the Jerusalem area, and the West Bank. Some missiles were intercepted, while others carried cluster bomb warheads, causing light injuries to three boys in Tel Sheva and two men in southern Israel from shrapnel/fragments. Hezbollah also fired rockets, with one striking a home in Kiryat Shmona, causing one light injury. The Home Front Command maintained existing civilian guidelines but indicated ongoing assessments for potential changes. Civilian aviation authorities announced Ben Gurion Airport (TLV) would return to full activity at midnight, while Ramon Airport (RMN) would open for domestic flights.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces killed Muhammad Dawad, a Hamas explosives expert involved in manufacturing explosive devices and planning attacks, in northern Gaza. There are no other detailed reports on ground operations, casualties, humanitarian situation, or settler activity in Gaza and the West Bank in the last 24 hours from the provided sources, beyond the general missile alerts covering these areas.

LEBANON
Lebanon experienced the most intense Israeli airstrikes since October 2023. The IDF conducted "Operation Eternal Darkness," its largest wave of strikes against Hezbollah infrastructure, hitting 100 targets in Beirut (Dahieh), Beqaa, and southern Lebanon (Sidon, Nabatieh, Tyre) within 10 minutes using 50 fighter jets. Lebanese Health Minister reported hundreds killed and injured across Lebanon. Specific targets included Hezbollah command centers, intelligence headquarters, rocket and naval units, and Radwan Force/aerial unit assets. Zadek al-Nablusi, brother of Hezbollah's former head of information Mohammed Afif, was killed in a strike in Sidon. A funeral procession in Beqaa was hit, killing at least 10. Four people were killed in an ambulance hit by Israeli forces in southern Lebanon. A vehicle was attacked in Al-Qasmiyah, and a building in Tyre was targeted after an evacuation warning. The emergency headquarters of Hezbollah's Secretary-General was among the targets, though his presence was unknown.

Hezbollah called on Lebanese civilians not to return to targeted areas until an official ceasefire announcement. While some Hezbollah officials stated they would not accept continued Israeli aggression and awaited negotiation outcomes, other sources close to Hezbollah indicated the group had halted fire on northern Israel as part of the US-Iran ceasefire. Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri claimed Lebanon was included in the ceasefire agreement, but Israel was violating it in southern Lebanon. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun welcomed the ceasefire and engaged in international contacts, including with French President Macron, to ensure Lebanon's inclusion. The Lebanese army urged civilians to avoid returning to southern villages due to ongoing Israeli attacks.

SYRIA & IRAQ
No specific reporting on Syria. In Iraq, Kata'ib Hezbollah announced the suspension of its military operations against occupying forces for a two-week period, following the US-Iran ceasefire. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced the release of American journalist Shelly Kittleson, kidnapped by Kata'ib Hezbollah in Iraq. Three Kata'ib Hezbollah members were reported killed. Reports indicated an attack on positions of the 19th Brigade of Hashd al-Shaabi in Sab' al-Bour, Baghdad. Tensions escalated between Iraq and Kuwait, with Hashd al-Shaabi supporters reportedly storming the Kuwaiti consulate in Basra after three Iraqis were killed in a missile attack attributed to Kuwaiti territory. Iraq reopened its airspace and airports.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's oil pipeline connecting the Caspian region to the Red Sea, a vital economic artery, was attacked around 13:00 local time, with one pumping station hit by a drone. The UAE Ministry of Defense reported its air defense systems intercepted 17 ballistic missiles and 35 drones launched from Iran, with a fire incident at the Habshan gas processing facility in Abu Dhabi. Kuwait's military intercepted 28 Iranian drones since 08:00, causing extensive material damage to vital oil facilities, power stations, and water desalination plants. Bahrain announced it intercepted six missiles and 31 drones. Qatar and Kuwait welcomed the US-Iran ceasefire and emphasized adherence to it. Oman's Transport Minister stated that agreements on maritime transport meant no fees would be imposed on Strait of Hormuz passage, contradicting an AP report about Iran and Oman charging transit fees during the ceasefire. Iran issued warnings to vessels in the Strait of Hormuz to seek IRGC Navy approval or face destruction. Iranian state media threatened that if Trump attacked Iran's power plants, Aramco and the UAE pipeline would be targets, and the electricity of all Gulf states would be cut.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran Ceasefire Declared:** US President Trump announced a two-week bilateral ceasefire with Iran, contingent on the full, immediate, and safe reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi confirmed they would halt defensive strikes if attacks stopped and would allow safe passage through Hormuz for two weeks.
2.  **Disputed Scope in Lebanon:** Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu stated the ceasefire does not include Lebanon, while Lebanese officials and Pakistan's PM Sharif asserted Lebanon's inclusion. This led to continued, extensive Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon.
3.  **Massive Israeli Strikes in Lebanon:** IDF launched "Operation Eternal Darkness," its largest wave of airstrikes against Hezbollah, using 50 fighter jets to hit 100 targets in Beirut, Beqaa, and southern Lebanon in 10 minutes. The Lebanese Health Minister reported hundreds of casualties.
4.  **Iranian Attacks on Gulf States Continue:** Despite ceasefire, Iran launched missile and drone attacks on UAE (17 ballistic, 35 drones intercepted), Kuwait (28 drones intercepted), Bahrain (6 missiles, 31 drones intercepted), and reportedly Saudi Arabia (oil pipeline pumping station).
5.  **Continued Iranian Missile Attacks on Israel:** Iran launched multiple ballistic missile attacks towards southern and central Israel, causing sirens in Tel Sheva, Beersheba, central Israel, Jerusalem area, and the West Bank. Some carried cluster warheads, causing light injuries.
6.  **Damage to Iranian Infrastructure:** IAF strikes targeted Iranian military production sites (Shiraz, Karaj) and key transport infrastructure, including 8 rail bridges/roads across multiple provinces (Tehran, Karaj, Tabriz, Kashan, Qom). The Lavan Island oil refinery was also attacked.
7.  **Strait of Hormuz Control:** Iran asserted its control over the Strait of Hormuz, demanding IRGC Navy approval for vessel passage and threatening to destroy unauthorized ships. However, FM Araghchi pledged "safe passage" for two weeks during the ceasefire.
8.  **Negotiations on 10-Point Plan:** Talks between the US and Iran are expected to begin on Friday, April 10, 2026, in Islamabad, Pakistan, based on Iran's 10-point proposal covering non-aggression, Hormuz control, uranium enrichment, sanctions removal, reparations, and US troop withdrawal.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The immediate risk of full-scale regional war has temporarily receded due to the US-Iran ceasefire, but significant escalation risks remain. Active flashpoints include Lebanon, where Israel continues aggressive strikes against Hezbollah, who in turn maintain readiness for retaliation. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint; despite Iran's pledge of safe passage, the demand for IRGC Navy authorization and previous threats of destruction signal potential for confrontation. Iranian attacks on Gulf States and continued missile launches towards Israel, even after the ceasefire announcement, demonstrate a fragile and highly conditional adherence to the truce. The threat of renewed or intensified Iranian retaliation against US/Israeli infrastructure if the ceasefire collapses, potentially including targeting power grids or oil infrastructure in the Gulf, is explicitly stated by Iran. Military posture changes are evident with both sides claiming readiness, and US warnings against bad-faith negotiations define clear red lines for the upcoming diplomatic phase.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States:** President Trump declared a "total and complete victory," stating US military objectives were achieved and Iran "begged for this ceasefire." He agreed to a two-week suspension of attacks contingent on the Strait of Hormuz reopening. VP Vance affirmed the US team would negotiate "in good faith" but warned Iran not to "mess with Trump" if they fail to do so. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on any country providing military aid to Iran. US military halted offensive operations but maintained defensive posture.
**Gulf States:** Kuwait and Qatar welcomed the ceasefire and urged full adherence. UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian missiles and drones. Saudi Arabia experienced an attack on its oil pipeline. Oman clarified that no fees would be imposed on Strait of Hormuz passage.
**Pakistan:** Prime Minister Sharif played a key mediating role, announcing the ceasefire and confirming Iran's participation in peace talks in Islamabad. He called for an immediate ceasefire "everywhere, including in Lebanon."
**China:** Credited by Trump and Iranian sources with intervention to encourage Iranian flexibility. China, along with Russia, vetoed a Bahraini-proposed UN Security Council resolution encouraging coordination on protecting commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
**Turkey:** President Erdogan welcomed the ceasefire and called for full implementation. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan held a phone call with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi regarding regional developments.
**European Union:** A joint statement from the UK, France, Germany, and the EU called for all parties to implement the ceasefire, "including in Lebanon." Spain's Foreign Minister condemned Israeli actions in Lebanon as "horrific and a crime" and emphasized Lebanon's inclusion in the ceasefire. France's President Macron would convene a defense council.
**Russia:** Welcomed the US-Iran decision to de-escalate militarily, hoping for direct contact between the two nations. Dmitry Medvedev, Deputy Chairman of Russia's Security Council, controversially called the Strait of Hormuz "Iran's nuclear weapon."
**Other:** UN Secretary-General Guterres welcomed the ceasefire. Pope Leo welcomed the truce. Egypt's Sisi thanked Trump for listening to "the voice of reason." Japan's PM Takayichi Sana spoke with President Pezeshkian, welcoming the ceasefire as a positive development.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist regarding the scope and nature of the ceasefire:
1.  **Lebanon's Inclusion:** Israel explicitly denies the ceasefire applies to Lebanon, while Lebanon's Parliament Speaker, President, and Pakistan's PM Sharif claim it does. Hezbollah is awaiting official confirmation and threatens retaliation if Israeli attacks continue. This is a critical gap that could easily reignite hostilities.
2.  **Ceasefire Adherence:** Despite the ceasefire announcement, Iranian sources reported continued missile and drone attacks on Gulf states, justifying them as retaliation for perceived US-Israeli attacks on Iranian oil facilities (Lavan, Sirri). Simultaneously, Iran launched multiple ballistic missiles at Israel post-ceasefire. This indicates either a lack of full control over all proxy forces, a deliberate strategy to test red lines, or a fundamental disagreement on the definition of "ceasefire" and "unprovoked attacks."
3.  **Iranian Claims of Victory:** Iranian officials universally portray the ceasefire as a "great victory" and a "strategic surrender" by the US, claiming Trump accepted their 10-point plan. Conversely, US officials (Trump, Vance, Leavitt) describe it as a "total and complete victory" for the US, having achieved military objectives and forcing Iran to the table. These diametrically opposed narratives are clear propaganda indicators, each designed to bolster internal legitimacy.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Transit Fees:** An AP report stated Iran and Oman would charge transit fees, but Oman's Transport Minister denied this, and Iran's Foreign Minister mentioned "safe passage... with technical limitations" and "coordination with Iranian armed forces," but no fees. This needs clarification, as fees could constitute an ongoing point of friction.
5.  **US "15 Points" vs. Iran's "10 Points":** Trump referred to "many of the 15 points already agreed upon," while Iran consistently refers to its "10-point plan." It is unclear if these refer to the same set of demands or if the US has its own set of demands that overlap with Iran's.
6.  **"Regime Change":** Trump's post stating the US will "work closely with Iran, a country that we have determined has gone through what will be a very productive regime change!" is highly inflammatory and contradictory to Iran's claims of an enduring Islamic Republic. Iran strongly denies any regime change. This phrase could derail negotiations.
7.  **Nuclear Material:** Trump claimed Iran's enriched uranium would be "perfectly handled" and that the US would work with Iran to "excavate and remove all 'nuclear dust'." This is vague and contradicts Iran's stated "acceptance of uranium enrichment" in its 10-point plan, highlighting a major reporting gap or fundamental disagreement on a core issue.
8.  **Internal Dissent:** Comments from Iranian hardliners (e.g., Hossein Shariatmadari calling ceasefire a "multi-sided gift to the enemy" and others calling for continued war) and reports of "disappointed" religious factions suggest internal divisions within Iran that could complicate adherence to any agreement. Similarly, Israeli opposition leader Lapid criticized Netanyahu's handling as a "political disaster."
